title: The Fortune Hunter

Throughout this opening section, we witness his deep struggles with inadequacy and his acute awareness of his failure to fit into the business world, contrasting sharply with the successes of others like his friend Harry Kellogg. Duncan’s interactions illustrate his charming yet tragic character as he tries to navigate the complexities of fate and friendship, leading to an intriguing yet daunting proposition by Kellogg: to marry for money. This twist sets the stage for a tale of ambition and moral inquiry, inviting readers to consider the costs of success and the definition of true fortune.
